statement: [DATO] Human SUMO-PDK1 is inhibited by AZD7545 with IC50 87 nM and human SUMO-PDK3 with IC50 600 nM in a radiolabel assay with E1p on the E2p/E3BP core (50 nM kinase, 50 uM ATP); curves plateau near 30% activity.

[DATO] Without the E2p/E3BP core AZD7545 does not inhibit but stimulates the isolated kinases (PDK1 1.3-fold, PDK3 10-fold at 10 uM), while with the core it leaves 28% (PDK1) and 31% (PDK3): the sign depends on the scaffold. [V1 correction: 'dual-role' is the authors' word for PDK3 only; PDK1 core-free 1.3-fold is called marginal (mean of two experiments, one concentration); PDK2 was not tested in the paper; the authors expect inhibition in situ because PDK3 is scaffold-bound]
[DATO] Core-free human PDK4 is stimulated about 2.8-fold by AZD7545 (kcat 98.3 against 35.1 per min, ratio recomputed) and binds it with a Kd of 48 nM that the paper cites as unpublished.

[DATO] The 2003 paper behind the repository's AZD7545 PDK1 7.43 and PDK2 8.19 (a Biochem Soc Trans symposium paper, abstract without numbers) was not reachable (Cloudflare 403), so species, construct, assay and the PDK2 number stay unverified; the later laboratory says its own PDK1 IC50 is more than 2-fold higher than that paper's.
locator: publisher page and PDF HTTP 403; Kato quote in evidence.tsv

statement: [INFERENZA] The repository's missing AZD7545 PDK3/PDK4 rows are not a 'not tested' gap of the field and must not be filled with 'inhibitor': both were measured later and the effect is activation without the E2 scaffold; whether the 2003 panel included them is unknown (paper not reached; perimeter: Kato 2007, Wynn 2008 and the VER-246608 paper). [V1 correction: justified for PDK4 only (core-free stimulation, no core-bound measurement); for PDK3 the measured core-bound inhibition (IC50 0.60 uM, 31% residual at 10 uM) may be recorded with its condition and the 10-fold core-free stimulation; not comparable with the 2003 PDK1 value]
locator: see A3D02-A3D03; VER paper Discussion on lipoamide-site compounds

statement: [DATO] VER-246608 inhibits four truncated His-tagged PDK constructs with IC50 35 (PDK-1), 84 (PDK-2, n=2), 40 (PDK-3) and 91 (PDK-4) nM in a DELFIA E1-substrate assay with 5 uM ATP and no E2; the repository pIC50 values are recomputations of these IC50 values; the paper does not name the enzyme species. [V1 correction: three truncated His-tagged constructs and one full-length (PDK-4, residues 1-412); PDK-4 enzyme 20 nM against 10 nM for the others; species unnamed (a residue-range hint of human PDK-1 and rodent PDK-4 is INFERENZA of the verifier)]

[DATO] VER-246608 competes with an ATP-site probe (FP IC50 79 nM), has a PDK-2 crystal structure in the ATP pocket and in human PC-3 cells lowers E1 alpha Ser293 phosphorylation (IC50 266 nM at 0% serum) and raises lysate PDH activity to about 138-148% of control (read off Fig 3A), with metabolic effects only under glucose-depleted conditions and when phosphorylation was almost abolished. [V1 correction: the 138-148% PDH activity is read off a raster bar: INFERENZA, not DATO]
locator: Results; Table 1; Figs 2 and 3 viewed; Fig 1 not viewed

statement: [INFERENZA] The AZD7545 and VER-246608 numbers must not be compared: different laboratories, different E2 content (core versus E1 only), ATP 50 versus 5 uM, readout (32P versus phospho-antibody), no shared isoform-assay pair, and a lipoamide-site compound changes sign with the substrate (AZD7545 A3D02; the VER paper's own Nov3r: stimulation in the E1 assay, IC50 3 nM with E1/E2).

[DATO] Dichloroacetate is a millimolar inhibitor of all isoforms tested in vitro and differs between them: apparent IC50 0.29 mM (basal) and 0.48 mM (core) for human PDK2; 40 mM leaves 4% (PDK1) and 28% (PDK3) with the core; Ki 0.2 mM (PDK2) to 8 mM (PDK3) in a 1998 rat-isoenzyme abstract (abstract only). [V1 correction: adds PDK4: 0.25 mM DCA lowers core-free kcat from 35.1 to 2.6 per min (Wynn 2008 Table 3); 'rat-isoenzyme' for the 1998 Ki is an inference, not in the abstract]

[DATO] DCA binds the helix bundle of the N-terminal (pyruvate-site) domain of PDK1, not the ATP pocket, and closes the kinase; enzyme inhibition (mM), cellular PDH activation (5-20 mM named by the VER paper) and clinical effect are three separate facts, and the brain/neural DCA results in this package's A2 table (tissue, cell lines, a peripheral-nerve myelination result) are copied, not reread; the MELAS trial finding (15 of 15 against 4 of 15 stopped, 17 of 19 stops for neuropathy) is copied at abstract level from the held INV-07 rows. [V1 correction: 'closes the kinase' belongs to the PDK2 and PDK4 structures, not to the PDK1 structure of Kato 2007]
source: Kato 2007 structure; Moore 2014 Discussion; held E29-E31

statement: [DATO] For celecoxib the source's own sentence says 'PDK1 (encoded by gene PDPK1)', for the GlcNAc-selenazoline and 3-hydroxyanthranilic-acid rows the linked papers concern insulin or T-cell signalling PDK1 (abstract or data-not-shown level), and the OSU-03012 row's identifier resolves to the dehydrogenase kinase while its pharmacology is PDPK1: four of the six non-typed DGIdb rows (OSU-03012, GlcNAc-selenazoline, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, celecoxib) concern the other kinase or an identifier clash, the dichloroacetic acid row concerns the dehydrogenase kinase, and devimistat lists the dehydrogenase kinases with no inhibitor evidence. [V1 correction: CHEMBL257158 is GlcNAc-thiazoline (sulfur, C8H13NO4S), not the selenazoline; the conclusion (PDK1 means PDPK1) is unchanged]

[DATO] Devimistat (CPI-613) is described as acting on the lipoate-using PDH and KGDH complexes; the sponsor-affiliated paper states the kinase link as stimulation of PDKs 1-4 (more inactivating PDH phosphorylation), so the four DGIdb PDK rows carry no inhibitor evidence and, if anything, the opposite sign.

[DATO] No typed row is the other kinase: ChEMBL's DCA record is the family target CHEMBL2096665 with UniProt Q15118, Q15119, Q15120, Q16654 (PDPK1 would be O15530); the GtoPdb target records for AZD7545 and VER-246608 could not be opened (login), so their identity rests on HGNC aliases (labelled fallback) and, for VER-246608, on the paper.

[DATO] The IT44 activity-only pointers (acid 4, nandrolone 4, sodium salt 12 rows) are one measurement per ChEMBL record fanned over the four components of the family target: nandrolone has one IC50 of 120 uM, the salt three family rows (two censored IC50 above 1 mM on porcine enzyme, one EC50 130 uM functional), the acid one censored IC50 above 2 mM (plus separate single-isoform rows from a 2017 document); the 1999-2000 papers behind them are not reachable and the target species recorded (human) differs from the porcine assay organism.
